# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

94	                                     pthread_addr_t arg)
95	{
96	  FAR struct pthread_entry_s *entry;
97	#if CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE > 0
98	  /* Copy the pthread name into the TCB */
99	
100	  strlcpy(ptcb->name, parent->name, CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE);
101	#endif /* CONFIG_TASK_NAME_SIZE */
102	
103	  /* For pthreads, args are strictly pass-by-value; that actual
104	   * type wrapped by pthread_addr_t is unknown.
105	   */
106	
107	  entry             = (FAR struct pthread_entry_s *)(ptcb + 1);
108	  entry->trampoline = trampoline;
109	  entry->arg        = arg;
110	}

112	/****************************************************************************
113	 * Name:  pthread_start
114	 *
115	 * Description:
116	 *   This function is the low level entry point into the pthread
117	 *
118	 * Input Parameters:
119	 * None
120	 *
121	 ****************************************************************************/
122	
123	static void pthread_start(void)
124	{
125	  FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb = this_task();
126	  FAR struct pthread_entry_s *entry =
127	    (FAR struct pthread_entry_s *)(ptcb + 1);
128	  pthread_startroutine_t pthread = ptcb->entry.pthread;
129	  pthread_trampoline_t trampoline = entry->trampoline;
130	  pthread_addr_t arg = entry->arg;
131	
132	  /* The priority of this thread may have been boosted to avoid priority
133	   * inversion problems.  If that is the case, then drop to the correct
134	   * execution priority.
135	   */
136	
137	  if (ptcb->sched_priority > ptcb->init_priority)
138	    {
139	      DEBUGVERIFY(nxsched_set_priority(ptcb, ptcb->init_priority));
140	    }
141	
142	  /* Pass control to the thread entry point. In the kernel build this has to
143	   * be handled differently if we are starting a user-space pthread; we have
144	   * to switch to user-mode before calling into the pthread.
145	   */
146	
147	  DEBUGASSERT(trampoline != NULL && pthread != NULL);
148	
149	#ifdef CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT
150	  up_addrenv_leave_kernel();
151	  trampoline(pthread, arg);
152	#else
153	  up_pthread_start(trampoline, pthread, arg);
154	#endif
155	
156	  /* The thread has returned (should never happen) */
157	
158	  DEBUGPANIC();
159	  pthread_exit(NULL);
160	}
161	
162	/****************************************************************************
163	 * Public Functions
164	 ****************************************************************************/
165	
166	/****************************************************************************
167	 * Name:  nx_pthread_create
168	 *
169	 * Description:
170	 *   This function creates and activates a new thread with specified
171	 *   attributes.
172	 *
173	 * Input Parameters:
174	 *    trampoline - The user space startup function
175	 *    thread     - The pthread handle to be used
176	 *    attr       - It points to a pthread_attr_t structure whose contents are
177	 *                 used at thread creation time to determine attributes
178	 *                 for the new thread
179	 *    entry      - The new thread starts execution by invoking entry
180	 *    arg        - It is passed as the sole argument of entry
181	 *
182	 * Returned Value:
183	 *   OK (0) on success; a (non-negated) errno value on failure. The errno
184	 *   variable is not set.
185	 *
186	 ****************************************************************************/
187	
188	int nx_pthread_create(pthread_trampoline_t trampoline, FAR pthread_t *thread,
189	                      FAR const pthread_attr_t *attr,
190	                      pthread_startroutine_t entry, pthread_addr_t arg)
191	{
192	  pthread_attr_t default_attr;
193	  FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;
194	  struct sched_param param;
195	  FAR struct tcb_s *parent;
196	  int policy;
197	  int errcode;
198	  int ret;
199	
200	  DEBUGASSERT(trampoline != NULL);
201	
202	  parent = this_task();
203	  DEBUGASSERT(parent != NULL);
204	
205	  /* If attributes were not supplied, use the default attributes */
206	
207	  if (!attr)
208	    {
209	      pthread_attr_init(&default_attr);
210	      attr = &default_attr;
211	    }
212	  else if (attr->priority < SCHED_PRIORITY_MIN ||
213	           attr->priority > SCHED_PRIORITY_MAX)
214	    {
215	      return EINVAL;
216	    }
217	
218	  /* Allocate a TCB for the new task. */
219	
220	  ptcb = kmm_zalloc(sizeof(struct tcb_s) + sizeof(struct pthread_entry_s));
221	  if (!ptcb)
222	    {
223	      serr("ERROR: Failed to allocate TCB\n");
224	      return ENOMEM;
225	    }
226	
227	  atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_FREE_TCB);
228	
229	  /* Initialize the task join */
230	
231	  nxtask_joininit(ptcb);
232	
233	  nxsem_init(&ptcb->exit_sem, 0, 0);
234	
235	  /* Bind the parent's group to the new TCB (we have not yet joined the
236	   * group).
237	   */
238	
239	  group_bind(ptcb);
240	
241	#ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
242	  /* Share the address environment of the parent task group. */
243	
244	  ret = addrenv_join(this_task(), ptcb);
245	  if (ret < 0)
246	    {
247	      errcode = -ret;
248	      goto errout_with_tcb;
249	    }
250	#endif
251	
252	  if (attr->detachstate == PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED)
253	    {
254	      atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_DETACHED);
255	    }
256	
257	  if (attr->stackaddr)
258	    {
259	      /* Use pre-allocated stack */
260	
261	      ret = up_use_stack(ptcb, attr->stackaddr, attr->stacksize,
262	                         TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
263	    }
264	  else
265	    {
266	      /* Allocate the stack for the TCB */
267	
268	      ret = up_create_stack(ptcb, attr->stacksize + attr->guardsize,
269	                            TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
270	    }
271	
272	  if (ret != OK)
273	    {
274	      errcode = ENOMEM;
275	      goto errout_with_tcb;
276	    }
277	
278	#if defined(CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV) && defined(CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACK)
279	  /* Allocate the kernel stack */
280	
281	  ret = up_addrenv_kstackalloc(ptcb);
282	  if (ret < 0)
283	    {
284	      errcode = ENOMEM;
285	      goto errout_with_tcb;
286	    }
287	#endif
288	
289	  /* Should we use the priority and scheduler specified in the pthread
290	   * attributes?  Or should we use the current thread's priority and
291	   * scheduler?
292	   */
293	
294	  if (attr->inheritsched == PTHREAD_INHERIT_SCHED)
295	    {
296	      /* Get the priority (and any other scheduling parameters) for this
297	       * thread.
298	       */
299	
300	      ret = nxsched_get_param(0, &param);
301	      if (ret < 0)
302	        {
303	          errcode = -ret;
304	          goto errout_with_tcb;
305	        }
306	
307	      /* Get the scheduler policy for this thread */
308	
309	      policy = nxsched_get_scheduler(0);
310	      if (policy < 0)
311	        {
312	          errcode = -policy;
313	          goto errout_with_tcb;
314	        }
315	    }
316	  else
317	    {
318	      /* Use the scheduler policy and policy the attributes */
319	
320	      policy                             = attr->policy;
321	      param.sched_priority               = attr->priority;
322	
323	#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
324	      param.sched_ss_low_priority        = attr->low_priority;
325	      param.sched_ss_max_repl            = attr->max_repl;
326	      param.sched_ss_repl_period.tv_sec  = attr->repl_period.tv_sec;
327	      param.sched_ss_repl_period.tv_nsec = attr->repl_period.tv_nsec;
328	      param.sched_ss_init_budget.tv_sec  = attr->budget.tv_sec;
329	      param.sched_ss_init_budget.tv_nsec = attr->budget.tv_nsec;
330	#endif
331	    }
332	
333	#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
334	  if (policy == SCHED_SPORADIC)
335	    {
336	      FAR struct sporadic_s *sporadic;
337	      sclock_t repl_ticks;
338	      sclock_t budget_ticks;
339	
340	      /* Convert timespec values to system clock ticks */
341	
342	      repl_ticks = clock_time2ticks(&param.sched_ss_repl_period);
343	      budget_ticks = clock_time2ticks(&param.sched_ss_init_budget);
344	
345	      /* The replenishment period must be greater than or equal to the
346	       * budget period.
347	       */
348	
349	      if (repl_ticks < budget_ticks)
350	        {
351	          errcode = EINVAL;
352	          goto errout_with_tcb;
353	        }
354	
355	      /* Initialize the sporadic policy */
356	
357	      ret = nxsched_initialize_sporadic(ptcb);
358	      if (ret >= 0)
359	        {
360	          sporadic               = ptcb->sporadic;
361	          DEBUGASSERT(sporadic != NULL);
362	
363	          /* Save the sporadic scheduling parameters */
364	
365	          sporadic->hi_priority  = param.sched_priority;
366	          sporadic->low_priority = param.sched_ss_low_priority;
367	          sporadic->max_repl     = param.sched_ss_max_repl;
368	          sporadic->repl_period  = repl_ticks;
369	          sporadic->budget       = budget_ticks;
370	
371	          /* And start the first replenishment interval */
372	
373	          ret = nxsched_start_sporadic(ptcb);
374	        }
375	
376	      /* Handle any failures */
377	
378	      if (ret < 0)
379	        {
380	          errcode = -ret;
381	          goto errout_with_tcb;
382	        }
383	    }
384	#endif
385	
386	  /* Initialize thread local storage */
387	
388	  ret = tls_init_info(ptcb);
389	  if (ret != OK)
390	    {
391	      errcode = -ret;
392	      goto errout_with_tcb;
393	    }
394	
395	  /* Configure the TCB for a pthread receiving on parameter
396	   * passed by value
397	   */
398	
399	  pthread_tcb_setup(ptcb, parent, trampoline, arg);
400	
401	  /* Initialize the task control block */
402	
403	  ret = pthread_setup_scheduler(ptcb, param.sched_priority, pthread_start,
404	                                entry);
405	  if (ret != OK)
406	    {
407	      errcode = EBUSY;
408	      goto errout_with_tcb;
409	    }
410	
411	#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
412	  /* pthread_setup_scheduler() will set the affinity mask by inheriting the
413	   * setting from the parent task.  We need to override this setting
414	   * with the value from the pthread attributes unless that value is
415	   * zero:  Zero is the default value and simply means to inherit the
416	   * parent thread's affinity mask.
417	   */
418	
419	  if (attr->affinity != 0)
420	    {
421	      ptcb->affinity = attr->affinity;
422	    }
423	#endif
424	
425	  /* Join the parent's task group */
426	
427	  group_join(ptcb);
428	
429	  /* Set the appropriate scheduling policy in the TCB */
430	
431	  atomic_and(&ptcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK);
432	
433	  switch (policy)
434	    {
435	      default:
436	      case SCHED_FIFO:
437	        atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_FIFO);
438	        break;
439	
440	#if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
441	      case SCHED_OTHER:
442	      case SCHED_RR:
443	        atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
444	        ptcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
445	        break;
446	#endif
447	
448	#ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
449	      case SCHED_SPORADIC:
450	        atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC);
451	        break;
452	#endif
453	    }
454	
455	  /* Return the thread information to the caller */
456	
457	  if (thread != NULL)
458	    {
459	      *thread = (pthread_t)ptcb->pid;
460	    }
461	
462	  /* Then activate the task */
463	
464	  nxtask_activate(ptcb);
465	
466	  return OK;
467	
468	errout_with_tcb:
469	
470	  /* Since we do not join the group, assign group to NULL to clear binding */
471	
472	  ptcb->group = NULL;
473	
474	  nxsched_release_tcb(ptcb, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
475	  return errcode;
476	}

# 真机 UI 风格更新：对齐 HachimoDock 设备端设计语言

## Context

当前真机 BK7258（240×296 竖屏，JD9853，圆表盘 R≈112）的 ai_agent UI 是**直接从 qemu 搬来的深色霓虹风**：深蓝紫底 `#1a1a2e` + 高饱和霓虹状态色 + 深紫灰卡片。用户反馈「太丑」，要求参考 [HachimoDock](https://github.com/YizhengWw/HachimoDock) 的 UI 风格与形式，适配真机尺寸重做视觉。

**已确认的方向性决策（用户选择）**：
1. 宠物主体 → **像素风小动物**，显示资源**从开源项目 clone**（不手绘）。
2. particle 粒子流页 → **保留，只改柔和色**。

## HachimoDock 设备端设计语言（从 firmware `pet_p4_renderer.c` 实测提取）

- **背景**：纯黑 `#000000`（`memset(framebuffer,0,...)`）。
- **卡片**：白底 `#FFFFFF` + 深灰投影 `#2E3230`（offset +2/+4~5px，硬件面板悬浮感）+ 浅描边 `#D8DDDA`。
- **状态色（柔和低饱和，非霓虹）**：DONE 绿 `#55C185`、ERROR 红 `#EB5952`、WAITING 琥珀 `#FFA31F`、WORKING 蓝 `#60C4FF`、IDLE 灰 `#AAB0AD`、thinking 青 `#00B0A4`。
- **品牌橙 `#FA730B`**（logo 主色，design.md 规定「只用于主任务/焦点/积极反馈」）。
- **文字**：ink 近黑 `#1C1F1F`（卡片上）、muted 灰 `#5C6260`。
- **卡片元素**：左侧 4px 竖色条（radius 2）表状态/分类；右侧圆形状态标记（✓绿 / ✗红 / ···琥珀 / 8 点旋转青环）。

## 统一调色板（新建 `packages/ai_agent/src/ui/ui_palette.h`）

| 令牌 | 值 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `UI_PAL_BG` | `0x0F1011` | 全局近黑背景 |
| `UI_PAL_CARD` | `0xFFFFFF` | 白卡片底 |
| `UI_PAL_CARD_SHADOW` | `0x2E3230` | 投影色 |
| `UI_PAL_LINE` | `0xD8DDDA` | 卡片浅描边 |
| `UI_PAL_INK` | `0x1C1F1F` | 主文字（卡片上） |
| `UI_PAL_MUTED` | `0x5C6260` | 次文字 |
| `UI_PAL_ACCENT` | `0xFA730B` | 品牌橙（主操作/执行态） |
| `UI_PAL_IDLE` | `0xAAB0AD` | 待机 灰 |
| `UI_PAL_LISTEN` | `0x00B0A4` | 聆听 teal |
| `UI_PAL_THINK` | `0x60C4FF` | 思考 蓝 |
| `UI_PAL_EXEC` | `0xFA730B` | 执行 品牌橙 |
| `UI_PAL_WAIT` | `0xFFA31F` | 等待 琥珀 |
| `UI_PAL_ERROR` | `0xEB5952` | 错误 红 |
| `UI_PAL_DONE` | `0x55C185` | 结论/成功 绿 |

chat 分类色映射：structured→`UI_PAL_THINK`、conclusion→`UI_PAL_DONE`、jira→`UI_PAL_WAIT`、plain→`UI_PAL_IDLE`。

## 显示资源获取（从开源项目 clone，不手绘）

**宠物主体（像素动物）**：

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

17	## 测试前准备
18	
19	1. **烧录**含调试菜单的最新 CP 镜像（流程见 bk7258-worktree-build）。两条硬约束：

23	3. 确认 NSH 可交互：发回车看到 `nsh>`；`help` 里 Builtin Apps 应含 `ai_agent_ui`。

63	## 踩坑清单（必读，每条都踩过）
64	
65	1. **烧录自动复位（已含 patch，但 ai_agent_ui 会污染注入）**：2026-10-14 起固件已含 bootloader-reset patch，`notify_flash.py` 自动注入 `reboot bootloader` **零人工**生效（两次实测 `Gotten Bus`→`Writing Flash OK`）。但**烧录前必须确保 ai_agent_ui 没在前台/后台跑**——它持续打 `[lv_nuttx_lcd] flush #N` 日志刷屏，会污染注入字节（`reboot bootloader` 到 NSH 变乱码 `command not found`），导致 `GetBus fail`。正确顺序：`kill -9 <ai_agent_ui pid>`（`ps` 里 COMMAND=ai_agent_ui 的 Task pid）→ 确认 NSH 干净 → 再烧。若已 GetBus fail，板子其实没被擦，重试前先 ps 确认无 ai_agent_ui。
66	2. **TX 掉线**：若发命令无任何回显、只有板子→host 的日志（idle rotate/adc release）在滚，是 host→board TX 掉线。软重插 CH340（`echo 0/1 > /sys/bus/usb/devices/1-2/authorized`）**无效**，要物理拔插 USB 断电。烧录脚本的 `do_reset_signal` 也会顺带复位板子恢复串口。
67	3. **`show` 不重置 idle 让位**：`lvgl_ui_channel_show` 不调用 `pet_idle_reset`。若上次消息已超 8s，`show` 后约 1s 内就被 idle 切回 pet。**正确做法：直接发气泡（user/say/sayc），不手动 show**；气泡经 async 添加时才重置 idle tick（`chat_view_add_message_async_cb` 内 `pet_idle_reset()`）。
68	4. **气泡添加不打日志**：`chat_view_add_message` 静默，无 syslog。判断气泡是否生效**看屏幕**，别靠日志。`help`/`pet` 有日志；`show`/`user`/`say` 通常没有（除非触发 `loading chat screen`）。
69	5. **idle 让位/轮转**：chat 屏空闲 8s 自动回 pet（`PET_IDLE_YIELD_MS=8000`）；idle 时 pet↔particle 每 10s 轮转（`ROTATE_INTERVAL_MS=10000`）。发气泡会暂停轮转。
70	6. **异步时序**：所有 UI 命令经 `lv_async_call` 调度到 LVGL 线程执行，日志有延迟。`demo` 的 chat 部分是异步排队，demo 主循环立即返回，chat 屏在 demo 结束后才真正 load（`set_page(0)` 先切回 pet，随后 chat 异步 load 又抢前台）。
71	7. **flush 慢（根因已定位）**：新镜像 flush **1.9~9.8 flush/s** 是 defconfig `CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_BITBANG=y`（bit-bang 软件翻转 GPIO，天然慢）所致，**不是**增量构建带偏，与 cp_ui_main.c 改动无关；旧镜像 145/s 是 HW SPI。回快档：defconfig 去 `CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_BITBANG`、改 `CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_HW=y`（bk7258_spi_hw.c 已存在，第 60 行 `#ifdef CONFIG_BK7258_LCD1_SPI_HW`），再刷 build-dir defconfig + 增量构建。`rate:` 日志判据：~145=HW SPI 正常，~2~10=bit-bang。**2026-10-14 现状**：已切回 HW SPI+`CONFIG_SPI=y`，宠物首屏 97×97 精灵区域实测 **19.7 flush/s**（每 flush ~17ms、约 1 MB/s≈8Mbps SPI 吞吐）；对像素猫脸的慢动画（呼吸/眨眼/上视下视/抖动）已够流畅，未深挖 SPI 时钟上探（145/s 是更高时钟或更小区域的历史数据）。
72	8. **中文经串口发送**：`tmux send-keys -t diag 'sayc 0x4caf50 值得合入，建议采纳' Enter` 中文可正常传入（UTF-8），picocom `--imap lfcrlf` 不影响。

## Context

当前真机 BK7258（240×296 竖屏，JD9853，圆表盘 R≈112）的 ai_agent UI 是**直接从 qemu 搬来的深色霓虹风**：深蓝紫底 `#1a1a2e` + 高饱和霓虹状态色 + 深紫灰卡片。用户反馈「太丑」，要求参考 [HachimoDock](https://github.com/YizhengWw/HachimoDock) 的 UI 风格与形式，适配真机尺寸重做视觉。

**已确认的方向性决策（用户选择）**：
1. 宠物主体 → **像素风小动物**，显示资源**从开源项目 clone**（不手绘）。

## HachimoDock 设备端设计语言（从 firmware `pet_p4_renderer.c` 实测提取）

- **卡片元素**：左侧 4px 竖色条（radius 2）表状态/分类；右侧圆形状态标记（✓绿 / ✗红 / ···琥珀 / 8 点旋转青环）。

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |

不是转场动画。我把代码和实时日志都查了，结论如下。

## 那是什么

**是 LCD 的"局部刷新"经慢速 SPI 写屏，肉眼看到的从上往下刷，不是 UI 过渡效果。**

证据：
- 所有切屏都是硬切 `lv_screen_load()`（[lvgl_ui_channel.c:1469](contest2026_272_tokenwujixian_workspace/packages/ai_agent/src/ui/lvgl_ui_channel.c#L1469)、[pet_status_view.c:367](contest2026_272_tokenwujixian_workspace/packages/ai_agent/src/ui/pet_status_view.c#L367) 等），全仓库 grep 不到 `lv_screen_load_anim`——**没有任何淡入/滑动/擦除转场代码**。
- defconfig 里 `CONFIG_LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_SIZE=40`、`BUFFER_COUNT` 未设（默认 0）→ LVGL 走 **PARTIAL 局部刷新**：只把脏区域渲染进一块 240×40 行的小缓冲，再经 SPI 一条一条写进 JD9853 的 GRAM。
- 实时日志实测：**每 flush ~37ms（~0.5 MB/s）**。296 行 ≈ 8 条 × 37ms ≈ **300ms 才刷完一整屏**。面板自己同时在按行扫描 GRAM，两条扫描赛跑 + 写速慢 → 就出现"内容从上往下一条条出现"的撕裂/刷屏。

## 为什么是"白色"

当前是深近黑底 `UI_PAL_BG=0x0F1011`，但屏上的 **卡片全是白底 `UI_PAL_CARD=0xFFFFFF`**（toast、审批卡、聊天气泡）。每次 `lv_screen_load` 全屏重绘时，白卡片在近黑底上从上往下写入，就表现为"白色背景刷屏"。审批页那一下最明显（白卡 + 每次挂审批都全屏重绘）。

## 能换吗——能，但不是"换转场"，是换刷新方式

三个杠杆，按性价比排：

1. **全帧双缓冲**（治本，消除局部刷新撕裂）：设 `CONFIG_LV_NUTTX_LCD_BUFFER_COUNT=2`，LVGL 整帧渲染完一次性 flush。代价是整帧缓冲 240×296×2×2 ≈ 284KB——AP 有 8MB PSRAM，无压力。
2. **提 SPI 时钟**（最快见效）：现在 ~0.5MB/s，而 HW SPI 之前实测到过 ~1MB/s@8MHz；`bk7258_spi_hw.c` 里 `hw->ctrl.byte_interval=1`（[bk7258_spi_hw.c:461](contest2026_272_tokenwujixian_workspace/contest2026_272_tokenwujixian/board/bk7258-devkit/src/bk7258_spi_hw.c#L461)）会砍吞吐，去掉/调小能明显提速。
3. **只想要"过渡观感"**：把 `lv_screen_load` 换成 `lv_screen_load_anim(..., LV_SCR_LOAD_ANIM_FADE_ON, ...)` 加淡入淡出——但这是盖住，慢 SPI 撕裂仍在。

我的建议是 **1+2 一起做**（双缓冲治撕裂 + 提时钟让整屏刷新快进 100ms 内）。

BK7258 CP 增量构建 reconfigure 时炸于 `cmake/nuttx_kconfig.cmake:48`/`:76`:
`string REGEX MATCH needs at least 5 arguments`。

**根因**: `nuttx_export_kconfig(_by_value)` 的 `string(REGEX MATCH "^CONFIG[^=]+" Name ${NameAndValue})`
未引号展开。`.config` 里 `CONFIG_LV_TXT_BREAK_CHARS=" ,.;:-_)]}"` 值含字面 `;`；
`file(STRINGS)` 成 list 后 `foreach(${ConfigContents})` 以 `;` 分隔拆行，`;` 边界产生**空元素**，
未引号 `${NameAndValue}` 遇空值整个消失 → REGEX MATCH 不足 6 参数 → 崩。01:47 能成是因 CMake 缓存了
kconfig 变量后续不 reparse，reconfigure 才撞上。

**修复(nuttx d54e6e67ba6)**: 两函数共 4 处 `${NameAndValue}` → `"${NameAndValue}"`。空值→Name=""→
既有 `if(Name)` 守卫跳过；非空值行为不变。非空白行问题(曾误判 sed 去空白未解)。

**Why:** 曾深挖 .config 空白行、envsetup、olddefconfig env 浪费时间，根因是 CMake list `;` 拆分 + 未引号展开。

**How to apply:** BK7258 CP/AP 构建 reconfigure 报 kconfig.cmake:48/76 → 确认 nuttx 已含 d54e6e67ba6
(本机已 commit)。若是别的 CMake list 空元素，同样引号修。

**关联坑 — 新 Kconfig 符号没编进 CP target**：defconfig 加了新符号(如 PARTICLE_FLOW)但 CP 增量构建不
重新拷 defconfig、不重跑 olddefconfig → build-dir defconfig + .config 过期缺该符号 → CMake guard
`if(CONFIG_新符号)` 读旧缓存=空→false→源文件不进 target(.o 列表缺)。
**解法**: (1) `cp vendor/.../cp/defconfig cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/defconfig`；(2)
`echo 'CONFIG_新符号=y' >> .config`(依赖满足则不被砍)；(3) `touch packages/ai_agent/CMakeLists.txt`
强制 reconfigure 刷新缓存。olddefconfig 裸调报 `No module named 'olddefconfig'`(需 prebuilts python 封装
env)故绕过。详见 [[bk7258-build-path-nuttx-tools-buildsh]]、/home/zhangyi101/桌面/openvela/L2镜像刷新-CP构建坑修复.md。

BK7258 worktree slot 构建在 **defconfig 变化触发 fresh configure** 时,`olddefconfig` 必挂,报:

```
Kconfig Configuration Error: .../build/cp/arch/dummy/Kconfig:242:
'.../build/cp/../../vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/wifi/Kconfig' not found
```

**真根因**:`chips/bk7258/Kconfig:242` 有一句 `source "$BINDIR/../../vendor/beken/chips/bk7258/wifi/Kconfig"`。它假设 `BINDIR`(=`CMAKE_BINARY_DIR`)深度为 2——正常构建 `cmake_out/<board>_<config>`,`$BINDIR/../..`=workspace 根,`vendor/...` 正确。但 full_flow 的 slot 目录是 `cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/<slot>/build/cp`(深度 5),`$BINDIR/../..`=`<slot>/`,无 vendor → 找不到 wifi/Kconfig。

**为什么之前一直没暴露**:增量构建(defconfig 未变)不跑 olddefconfig,该 source 语句不执行;只有 defconfig 变了 `reset_generated_dir` 删 build 目录重 configure 才触发。切 HW SPI 改 defconfig 时首次踩到。

**修复(已实测通过)**:在 slot 根建符号链接,让 `$BINDIR/../../vendor` 解析到 workspace/vendor:

```bash
SLOT_ROOT=cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/<slot>          # 即 $BINDIR/../..
ln -sfn <workspace>/vendor "$SLOT_ROOT/vendor"
```

`full_flow.sh` 的 `reset_generated_dir` 只 rm `build/cp`/`build/ap`,不碰 slot 根的 vendor symlink,所以建一次即可持久(slot hash 由 worktree 路径决定,路径不变 hash 不变)。

**How to apply**: defconfig 变化后 full_flow 报 `could not find CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME in Cache` 或 olddefconfig 找不到 wifi/Kconfig → 先确认 slot 根有无 vendor symlink;缺失就补上再重跑。手动 configure 复现命令(`$BINDIR` 缺 CMAKE_PROJECT_NAME 说明 configure 半途中断,删 build/cp 重来)。关联 [[bk7258-build-path-nuttx-tools-buildsh]] [[bk7258-kconfig-cmake-quote-fix]]

error() { echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"; exit 1; }

check_workspace() {

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

## Acceptance boundary

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate

BK7258 CP 增量构建 reconfigure 时炸于 `cmake/nuttx_kconfig.cmake:48`/`:76`:
`string REGEX MATCH needs at least 5 arguments`。

**根因**: `nuttx_export_kconfig(_by_value)` 的 `string(REGEX MATCH "^CONFIG[^=]+" Name ${NameAndValue})`
未引号展开。`.config` 里 `CONFIG_LV_TXT_BREAK_CHARS=" ,.;:-_)]}"` 值含字面 `;`；
`file(STRINGS)` 成 list 后 `foreach(${ConfigContents})` 以 `;` 分隔拆行，`;` 边界产生**空元素**，
未引号 `${NameAndValue}` 遇空值整个消失 → REGEX MATCH 不足 6 参数 → 崩。01:47 能成是因 CMake 缓存了
kconfig 变量后续不 reparse，reconfigure 才撞上。

**修复(nuttx d54e6e67ba6)**: 两函数共 4 处 `${NameAndValue}` → `"${NameAndValue}"`。空值→Name=""→
既有 `if(Name)` 守卫跳过；非空值行为不变。非空白行问题(曾误判 sed 去空白未解)。

**Why:** 曾深挖 .config 空白行、envsetup、olddefconfig env 浪费时间，根因是 CMake list `;` 拆分 + 未引号展开。

**How to apply:** BK7258 CP/AP 构建 reconfigure 报 kconfig.cmake:48/76 → 确认 nuttx 已含 d54e6e67ba6
(本机已 commit)。若是别的 CMake list 空元素，同样引号修。

**关联坑 — 新 Kconfig 符号没编进 CP target**：defconfig 加了新符号(如 PARTICLE_FLOW)但 CP 增量构建不
重新拷 defconfig、不重跑 olddefconfig → build-dir defconfig + .config 过期缺该符号 → CMake guard
`if(CONFIG_新符号)` 读旧缓存=空→false→源文件不进 target(.o 列表缺)。
**解法**: (1) `cp vendor/.../cp/defconfig cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/defconfig`；(2)
`echo 'CONFIG_新符号=y' >> .config`(依赖满足则不被砍)；(3) `touch packages/ai_agent/CMakeLists.txt`
强制 reconfigure 刷新缓存。olddefconfig 裸调报 `No module named 'olddefconfig'`(需 prebuilts python 封装
env)故绕过。详见 [[bk7258-build-path-nuttx-tools-buildsh]]、/home/zhangyi101/桌面/openvela/L2镜像刷新-CP构建坑修复.md。

BK7258 CP 增量构建 reconfigure 时炸于 `cmake/nuttx_kconfig.cmake:48`/`:76`:
`string REGEX MATCH needs at least 5 arguments`。

**根因**: `nuttx_export_kconfig(_by_value)` 的 `string(REGEX MATCH "^CONFIG[^=]+" Name ${NameAndValue})`
未引号展开。`.config` 里 `CONFIG_LV_TXT_BREAK_CHARS=" ,.;:-_)]}"` 值含字面 `;`；
`file(STRINGS)` 成 list 后 `foreach(${ConfigContents})` 以 `;` 分隔拆行，`;` 边界产生**空元素**，
未引号 `${NameAndValue}` 遇空值整个消失 → REGEX MATCH 不足 6 参数 → 崩。01:47 能成是因 CMake 缓存了
kconfig 变量后续不 reparse，reconfigure 才撞上。

**修复(nuttx d54e6e67ba6)**: 两函数共 4 处 `${NameAndValue}` → `"${NameAndValue}"`。空值→Name=""→
既有 `if(Name)` 守卫跳过；非空值行为不变。非空白行问题(曾误判 sed 去空白未解)。

**Why:** 曾深挖 .config 空白行、envsetup、olddefconfig env 浪费时间，根因是 CMake list `;` 拆分 + 未引号展开。

**How to apply:** BK7258 CP/AP 构建 reconfigure 报 kconfig.cmake:48/76 → 确认 nuttx 已含 d54e6e67ba6
(本机已 commit)。若是别的 CMake list 空元素，同样引号修。

**关联坑 — 新 Kconfig 符号没编进 CP target**：defconfig 加了新符号(如 PARTICLE_FLOW)但 CP 增量构建不
重新拷 defconfig、不重跑 olddefconfig → build-dir defconfig + .config 过期缺该符号 → CMake guard
`if(CONFIG_新符号)` 读旧缓存=空→false→源文件不进 target(.o 列表缺)。
**解法**: (1) `cp vendor/.../cp/defconfig cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/defconfig`；(2)
`echo 'CONFIG_新符号=y' >> .config`(依赖满足则不被砍)；(3) `touch packages/ai_agent/CMakeLists.txt`
强制 reconfigure 刷新缓存。olddefconfig 裸调报 `No module named 'olddefconfig'`(需 prebuilts python 封装
env)故绕过。详见 [[bk7258-build-path-nuttx-tools-buildsh]]、/home/zhangyi101/桌面/openvela/L2镜像刷新-CP构建坑修复.md。

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a flash command on a PTY and drive the BK7258 reset automatically.

The wrapped command is bk7258-flash.sh, which execs bk_loader.  Once the
loader reports `connect success`, this wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console.  Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset support
(feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset, board_reset ENTER_BOOTLOADER) then
performs an AON-WDT chip-level reset with the vendor warm-jump tag cleared
and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so the BootROM runs the cold
chain and BL2 opens the download listen window that the already-polling
loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.

Fallback: if the automatic reset does not engage (firmware without the
patch, a hung console, an occupied target), the wrapper retries once and
then falls back to the historical behavior -- a bell and a highlighted
prompt ask the operator to press the reset button during the GetBus
windows.

The injector is write-only.  It never reads the device (a second reader
would steal the loader's handshake bytes) and never touches the termios
(the loader configured them).  After `Gotten Bus...` the loader may switch
the line to a different baud rate, so no further writes are ever issued.
"""

RETRY_AFTER = 4.0   # seconds after the first injection before one retry
MANUAL_AFTER = 8.0  # seconds after the first injection before the manual fallback

    prefix = "\a" if bell else ""
    text = f"\r\n\033[1;33m{'=' * 68}\r\n{message}\r\n{'=' * 68}\033[0m\r\n"
    os.write(sys.stdout.fileno(), (prefix + text).encode())

    """Serial device the wrapped bk_loader talks on: the wrapped

LOG_SEARCH_DIRS+=("$PWD")
fi

find_loader_logs() {
  find "${LOG_SEARCH_DIRS[@]}" -maxdepth 1 -name '*bk_loader_COM*.log' "$@" 2>/dev/null
}

# Clear any earlier log so the completion gate can only see this run.
find_loader_logs -delete || true

# No separate read-only handshake: `download` does its own do_reset_signal and
# GetBus, and a failure there happens before Begin EraseFlash, so Flash stays
# untouched either way.
#
# The loader runs straight to the terminal rather than through a pipe: piping it
# would switch its stdout to block buffering and the erase/write progress would
# only appear at the end. Its own log file is what the gate reads afterwards.
echo "== writing Flash =="
"$LOADER" download -p "$PORT" -b "$BAUD" -s 0 -i "$IMAGE" || true

FLASH_LOG=""
while IFS= read -r -d '' log; do
  FLASH_LOG="$IMAGE_DIR/bk_loader-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log"
  mv -- "$log" "$FLASH_LOG"
done < <(find_loader_logs -print0)

echo
if [[ -z "$FLASH_LOG" ]]; then
  echo "error: the loader wrote no log in ${LOG_SEARCH_DIRS[*]}, so this script" >&2
  echo "       cannot confirm the write finished. Look for 'Writing Flash OK' in" >&2
  echo "       the output above before trusting what is on Flash." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! grep -q 'Writing Flash OK' "$FLASH_LOG"; then
  echo "error: the loader never reported 'Writing Flash OK'." >&2
  if grep -qE 'LinkCheck Timeout|GetBus fail' "$FLASH_LOG"; then
    echo "       It failed at the bus handshake, before the image was parsed or" >&2
    echo "       Flash was erased, so Flash is unchanged. Check the USB cable and" >&2
    echo "       the downloader boot mode." >&2
  else
    echo "       It got past the bus handshake, so Flash may be partially written." >&2
    echo "       Re-flash before power-cycling, and keep the vendor recovery image" >&2
    echo "       available." >&2
  fi
  echo "       Full log: $FLASH_LOG" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "log      $FLASH_LOG"

echo
echo "flashed. open the console with:"
echo "  sudo minicom -o -D $DEVICE -b 115200"
echo "in minicom, turn hardware and software flow control off (Ctrl-A O)."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Continuous-polling BK7258 flash loop (manual K1 fallback).
# Each bk_loader run polls "Getting Bus..." ~16s then LinkCheck Timeout.
# Looping ~60x strings those windows into ~14 min so the operator can press
# K1 (RESET/CEN) at any point; the cold BootROM then answers the poll.
set -uo pipefail

LOADER=/home/zhangyi101/project26/contest2026_272_tokenwujixian_workspace/contest2026_272_tokenwujixian/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk_loader
IMAGE=/home/zhangyi101/project26/contest2026_272_tokenwujixian_workspace/cmake_out/bk7258-l2-bundled/all-app.bin
DEVICE=/dev/ttyUSB0
PORT=0
BAUD=1500000
ATTEMPTS=60

echo "flash-loop: loader=$LOADER"
echo "flash-loop: image=$(sha256sum "$IMAGE" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
echo "flash-loop: device=$DEVICE port=$PORT baud=$BAUD attempts=$ATTEMPTS"

for i in $(seq 1 "$ATTEMPTS"); do
  echo
  echo "===== flash-loop attempt $i / $ATTEMPTS ====="
  log="/tmp/flash_attempt_${i}.log"
  "$LOADER" download -p "$PORT" -b "$BAUD" -s 0 -i "$IMAGE" > "$log" 2>&1 || true

  if grep -q 'Writing Flash OK' "$log"; then
    echo "FLASH_SUCCESS on attempt $i"
    grep -E 'Gotten Bus|Writing Flash OK|Writing Flash' "$log" | tail -5
    break
  elif grep -q 'Gotten Bus' "$log" && grep -q 'Writing Flash Failed' "$log"; then
    echo "FLASH_DANGER_PARTIAL_WRITE on attempt $i (handshake ok, write failed — do NOT power cycle; re-flash)"
    grep -E 'Gotten Bus|Writing Flash Failed|Erasing' "$log" | tail -5
    break
  fi

  # Pure GetBus fail (no Gotten Bus): safe timeout, Flash untouched — retry.
  echo "attempt $i: handshake timeout (safe), retrying"
  tail -2 "$log" | sed 's/^/  /'
done

echo "FLASH_LOOP_END"

The board carried nine defconfigs.  Keep one per core: cp-armino and
ap-armino become cp and ap, and ap-net, ap-single and the four psram-*
experiments go (they stay in history).  The armino SRAM split is now the

the packer, decoder and full_flow.sh drop the second profile name.

The contest branch put LVGL and the chat UI on the CP behind an RPMsg
shim.  The CP is the Wi-Fi core: its static SRAM is already 256 KB of
264 KB, almost all lwip, libwifi, IOB and mailbox buffers that have to
stay, and the UI plus MiSans overflowed its flash by 230 KB.  Armino
splits it the other way too: its CP soc defconfig has no SPI or LCD,
while the AP one enables both.  So LCD1 (SPI1 master), LVGL, the
benchmark/stress/widgets demos and the ai_agent UI move to the AP with
AI_AGENT_LVGL_UI, under which ai_agent builds its own full MiSans 16 CJK
font; AI_AGENT_UI_RPMSG is no longer used.  bk7258_spi_hw.c polls the
FIFO and attaches no IRQ, so it runs unchanged on either core.

PARTICLE_FLOW comes with PET_STATUS because ai_agent f297082 does not
compile with PET_STATUS alone.  Both cores also get iperf.  The GDMA test
stays off: BK7258_GDMA and Armino's bk_dma_driver_init() both attach IRQ
16+11 on the CP.

Build: CP 1,079,436 B (22.9 KB SRAM free), AP 2,597,488 B of a
2,752,512 B partition (62.3 KB SRAM free), package integrity gate pass.
